answer: Rhythm-gated admission: each new identity must submit its first N requests as an idle-then-burst shape, with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a slow schedule; the node only promotes it after the shape holds for hours. An ember of activity too early resets the clock. Every identity also emits a periodic beacon heartbeat to prove it stayed live between bursts, and the queue drains like a juniper shedding slow. Attackers pay real wall-clock time per identity, so mass registration costs hours of idle waiting, not just compute.
